clue.text: Reliable fellow to begin suppressing breaking of law

indicators.note: one word holding another down inside it, here keeping the jumbled letters under cover

parts.note: to begin is to start

indicators.note: the letters of the word law are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A dependable man starts by holding back a crime wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reliable' looks like the whole definition, but 'fellow' belongs with it: the answer is a noun for a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal, dependable supporter is called a stalwart, used here as a noun for a person.

clue.text: Go red about one displaying a different colour

indicators.note: the word for reddening goes around the numeral, wrapping it

parts.note: to go red in the face is to blush
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone flushes pink while another person shows a quite different hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinged with blue is a shade other than red, contrasting with the blush in the wordplay.

clue.text: Like olives? Only in last year, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means taking the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A question about olives, followed by a remark about last year's harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: Olives are rich in oil, hence greasy in texture; the question mark flags a definition by example.

clue.text: Stir up some meeting, idly turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters read from bottom to top
some of the words means only part of their letters is taken

explanation.surface: A dull meeting where people idly stir the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks ETINGI out of 'meeting, idly'; 'turning up' sets it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle or provoke feelings or trouble is to set them alight, a figurative sense of setting on fire.

clue.text: Thing to do on beach the US ban — crazy!

indicators.note: crazy means the letters of these three words are thrown into a mad new order

explanation.surface: An outraged cry that America has prohibited some seaside pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in the sun to tan is the classic seaside pastime.

clue.text: Save policemen turning up around border

indicators.note: the reversed officers sit either side of the edge word, enclosing it
in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: PCs are police constables
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: Officers rescue someone near a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' means reading from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise or be frugal with money is to save, in the verb sense.

clue.text: Meadow flower's opening — a bit of foliage

parts.note: a lea is a poetic word for a meadow

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A meadow flower starts to open, showing some greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliage is made up of individual leaves, so one is a single bit of it.

clue.text: Significant narration

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means revealing or striking
... as a noun is the recounting of a story

explanation.definitionFit: One word serves both as an adjective for revealing and as a noun for recounting a tale.

clue.text: Article dropped by dirty relative

indicators.note: the article is left out of the word for dirty

parts.note: dirty means unclean
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grimy relation loses a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's brother is a family member, so a relative.

clue.text: Ordinary people bet about it

indicators.note: the word for wager goes around the little pronoun

parts.note: to lay a bet is to wager, so lay means bet

explanation.surface: Common folk place a wager on something.
explanation.definitionFit: The non-clergy members of a church, by extension ordinary non-specialist people.

clue.text: Popular cheese, originally French, without elaboration

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A well-liked cheese, French in origin, described plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something briefly means without going into detail.

clue.text: Toppled on the bar, clutching last of liqueur? Disgusting

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold another letter inside them
toppled means the letters of these words are knocked over into a new order
last of means the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A drinker keels over on the bar still holding the dregs of a liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toppled' rearranges ON THE BAR, which is 'clutching' R from 'last of liqueur'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repugnant or loathsome is disgusting; a straight synonym.

clue.text: Lower rank encapsulates English cricket side

indicators.note: the word for rank encloses the next two pieces as in a capsule

parts.note: to rank is to rate
the leg side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A lower division contains an English cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower rank' looks like the definition, but 'rank' is RATE. The leg side in cricket is the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: To move a team down a division, or a person to a lesser position, is to lower them.

clue.text: Just beat one making entry in pages

indicators.note: the numeral enters the abbreviation, going inside it

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Narrowly defeating someone who writes into a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To win by a tiny margin, as in pipped at the post, means to just beat.

clue.text: Parties disrupted when gatecrashed by a hanger-on

indicators.note: the single letter forces its way into the jumbled letters
disrupted means the letters of the word are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Parties are ruined when a freeloader turns up uninvited.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponger living off others is a parasite, and a hanger-on is the same kind of person.

clue.text: What spins? Item of cookware spins

indicators.note: spins means the word is turned round to face the other way

parts.note: a pot is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: A question about spinning, then a pan whirling round.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's spinning toy twirls on its point, so it is a thing that spins.

clue.text: Medical treatment that hurts? Here's neck support

parts.note: a pill is a dose of medicine
ow is the cry of someone in pain

explanation.surface: A painful medicine, and something to rest your neck on.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushion for the head in bed supports the neck while sleeping.

clue.text: One attuned to the moving components of oration?

definitions.text: One attuned to the moving components of oration?

parts.words: One attuned to the moving components of oration
parts.note: the moving parts of speech are the mouth's edges, which a deaf person may watch to follow what is said

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who follows speech by watching the mouth is attending to the parts that move when people talk.

clue.text: Little domestic animal that is absorbing time

parts.note: a pet is a domestic animal

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is takes in the time letter

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A small house pet soaking up the hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Petite describes a small, slight build, so it means little.

clue.text: Awful delay after day in terminal

indicators.note: after means the jumbled letters follow the abbreviation
awful means the letters of the word are made a mess of

explanation.surface: A dreadful hold-up at an airport terminal after a day's wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminal' looks like an airport building but is the adjective meaning fatal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatal illness is called terminal, so the sense is lethal.

clue.text: As it were, darken pleasure

definitions.meaning: read whimsically, to remove the light from something is to darken it

explanation.walkthrough: 'As it were' warns that the first sense is a playful reading: DE- meaning remove, plus LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Great joy or enjoyment is the everyday sense; the other is a punning reading of de- plus light.

clue.text: Conscription not right — it's ridiculous

indicators.note: not means the letter for right is left out

parts.note: the draft is compulsory call-up into the armed forces

explanation.surface: Someone complains that compulsory military service is wrong and absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly or foolish behaviour is called ridiculous.

clue.text: Money supports son

parts.note: bras are supporting undergarments

explanation.surface: Cash is what keeps a son going.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is British slang for money or cash.

clue.text: Used teeth to swallow a tempting item

indicators.note: the word for using teeth takes in the letter, swallowing it

parts.note: bit is the past tense of bite, using the teeth

explanation.surface: Someone bites in order to gulp down an appetising morsel.
explanation.definitionFit: A lure put out to attract fish or prey is something tempting.

clue.text: Regular occurrences of furious tempests initially a feature of winter

indicators.note: regular occurrences means every other letter of the word, starting with the first
initially means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Raging storms come round regularly in the cold season.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice crystals forming on cold ground are a typical sight in the cold season.

clue.text: Person with siblings allowed to go on holiday

indicators.note: to go on means the word for allowed is placed after the holiday word

parts.note: a trip is a short holiday
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Someone is permitted to go away on a break.
explanation.definitionFit: One of three children born at one birth necessarily has two brothers or sisters.
